Exchanges the four pages at $BC00-$BFFF with $DC00-$DFFF, with every ROM and the I/O banked out ($01 = $34), and banks the KERNAL back in ($01 = $36).

Every event calls this on the way out, with $02 = the event (0 Slither, 1 Hockey, 2 Judo, 3 Head Throwing, 4 Marathon, or 5 at a championship's end, which checks all five): points the NMI and IRQ vectors at an RTI, reads a key to clear it, sets up a text screen (video bank 0, screen $0400, characters $0800, sprites off, black), checks the records ($D005), shows them ($D32D), keeps the new ones ($D77D), and at a championship's end shows the closing title ($C540 with A = 5).
Meant to silence the sound and keep the filter bits, but ANDs with the byte at $F0 rather than the number $F0, and reads $D418, which the SID only lets programs write.

Who broke each event's record, by event: 0 nobody, 1 player one, 2 player two.
Clears records_changed and checks event $02's records (0 to 4), or all five at a championship's end (5).

100m Slither: lower is better. With $B809 set, moves player two's time to player one's place. Player one's time under the record makes them the holder; player two's under it does too, unless player one's is lower still. The holder's time goes to $BC82.
Space Hockey: higher is better, one byte. With $B812 set, moves player two's goals to player one's place. The holder is found as for Slither, and the goals go to $BC84.
Psychic Judo: lower is better, three bytes; $99 $99 means no time. With $B823 set, moves player two's time to player one's place. The holder's time goes to $BC86-$BC88.
Head Throwing: higher is better. With $B82C set, player two's distance is dropped. The holder's distance goes to $BC88.
The Marathon: lower is better; player two is left out when $B82F is $0F. The holder's time goes to $BC8A.
Carry clear when the two-byte decimal number at ($03) is less than the one at ($05).
The same for three-byte numbers.
Carry clear when the two-byte decimal number at ($03) is more than the one at ($05).
The same for one byte.
print_rle's run count.

The records screen: copies its font to $0900 ($BC96), clears the screen in white and prints the table ($B970); then each event's two results and record: Slither, Head Throwing and the Marathon as two pairs of digits with a colon, Hockey as two digits, Judo with its minute first (the record without it); "-" fills a missing one. Flashes the new records ($D4D9) until a key or fire, fades out ($D75F) and waits 20 frames. At a championship's end it goes on: the championship screen ($BB48), the points worked out ($AD0C, in the Marathon's file), printed ($D5D5), the champion crowned ($D619), and a fade.
Prints the low digit of the byte at ($03) and a colon, unless the byte is $FF or that digit is 0.
Prints the byte at ($03) as two digits, or "--" for $FF.
Prints the two bytes at ($03) as two pairs of digits with a colon, high byte first, or "-----" when the high byte is $FF.
The five dashes.
Prints the three values in the pointer list at ($05): player one's, player two's and the record.
Takes the next pointer from the list at ($05) into $03.
Prints A as two decimal digits.
Writes A at the screen place in its operand ($D4CE/$D4CF) and moves on one.
put_char's screen place, low byte.
put_char's screen place, high byte.

Flashes the new records until a key or fire: every 8 or 16 frames, turns $0A between black and white and colours the holder's result (nine cells) and the record (seven) of each event with a new record.
The ASCII code for each key code below $3D, 0 for the keys it ignores: RETURN gives $0D, the left arrow $1B, and the letters, digits and space themselves.
The key just pressed, as ASCII ($D545): 0 when none is, or while the same key is held; codes from $3D up come back as they are.
A new key: through the table when it has an entry.
Prints run-length text from the address in its LDA ($D5CB) to the screen at ($03): $C8 n c puts n copies of c, $FF ends.
The next byte of the text, moving the address on.
The text's address, low byte.
The text's address, high byte.
Prints the two players' championship points at $0554 and $05CC, or "----" for a player without any.
Prints four dashes.
Prints X dashes.

The champion: each player's points, unless there are none, are compared with the champion's record ($BC8C) and with each other's. When one beats the record, prints "CONGRATULATIONS PLAYER n..." ($BBE4), keeps the points, marks the records changed, and takes a name of up to eight characters over underscores, the points flashing ($B928): ← deletes, RETURN pads it with spaces, and a key after the eighth character ends it. Otherwise prints the champion's name and record ($BB9C) and waits for a key.
Nobody beat the record: the champion and their record.
Prints the name being entered at $073A.
Prints the eight characters at $BC8E at put_char's place.
Reads a key to clear it, then fades the screen through light grey, grey and dark grey to black, two frames each ($D773).
Waits two frames and fills colour RAM with Y.
For each event with a new holder, copies two bytes of its new record ($BC82 on) over the record ($BC64 on, six bytes an event) and clears the holder. Judo's third byte is not copied.
Sets put_char's place from bytes 4 and 5 of the value at ($03): each result and record keeps its own place there.
For each event, pointers to player one's result, player two's and the record: Slither here, Hockey at $D7DD, Judo at $D7E3, Head Throwing at $D7E9 and the Marathon at $D7EF.
Space Hockey's pointers: $B80A, $B80C, $BC6A.
The pointer to player two's Space Hockey goals.
The pointer to the Space Hockey record.
Psychic Judo's pointers, at the minutes bytes of player one's time ($B815) and player two's ($B81D), and the record ($BC70).
The pointer to player two's Judo minutes.
The pointer to the Judo record.
Head Throwing's pointers: $B824, $B826, $BC76.
The Marathon's pointers: $B82D, $B82F, $BC7C.
Each event's row in colour RAM, for flash_records: $0124, $019C, $0214, $028C, $0304 on from $D800.
The high byte of the Slither row's place in colour RAM.
A byte after flash_rows that nothing reads.
The fast loader, kept here under the I/O and swapped to $BC00 for each load ($0819), so its own addresses read $BC00 on: this first byte is JMP $BE31, which installs it.

The drive's half, which runs in the 1541 at $0600-$071B: follows the file's chain of sectors, finding each header ($F934) and decoding the sector ($F8E0) through the drive's own ROM, steps the head itself between tracks, and sends each sector's bytes, a count first, to the computer ($06CD).
In the drive at $06CD: sends a byte to the computer two bits at a time over the serial bus's clock and data lines, a nibble at a time through the table at $0708.
In the drive at $0708: each nibble's bit pairs as drive_send puts them on the bus.
In the drive at $0718: the bit-rate bits for each of the disk's four speed zones.

In the drive at $071C, written with M-W and started with M-E: takes the rest of the drive code over the bus into $0600-$071B ($0750), has the drive's job loop run it (job $E0 for the buffer at $0600), and when that ends jumps into the drive's ROM at $D048.
In the drive at $0750: takes a byte from the computer, two bits at a time.
In the computer at $BD85: takes a byte from the drive two bits at a time through $DD00, waiting first for a raster line where no bad line can fall inside the transfer.
In the computer at $BDC3: sends a byte to the drive two bits at a time, nibble by nibble through the table at $BE11.
In the computer at $BE11: each nibble's bit pattern for $DD00, then sixteen bytes in the reverse order that nothing reads.
At $BE31: points the KERNAL's LOAD vector ($0330) at $BE3C.

At $BE3C, the LOAD itself: opens the file by name through the KERNAL's serial routines, takes the KERNAL's FILE NOT FOUND exit when the drive does not answer (status bit 1), writes drive_boot into the drive in 32-byte M-W commands and starts it with M-E, sends the drive code, then takes the file block by block: a count before each block ($FF an error, 0 the end), the load address first. It stores with the ROMs and I/O banked out, so a file can load anywhere, and returns like the KERNAL: carry clear, status $40 and the end address in X and Y.
The next block: its count.
The drive reported an error: carry set and error 4, FILE NOT FOUND.
At $BF46: the $DD00 values for the transfer and the raster window get_byte waits for.
At $BF60: opens the drive's command channel and sends "M-" and the letter in A (W or E).
Left over after the loader: a line of assembler source ("STA" between tabs), then repeating groups of thirteen bytes like those at $E000.
The title screens' hi-res bitmap, $E000-$FF3F, cleared ($CA13) and starred each time a title shows. Between titles it holds what the boot left: here thirteen-byte groups that repeat.
Left from the boot: an earlier build of the records code at $B839 on, the same bytes $292F higher.
Left from the boot: an earlier copy of the records table's text ($B970).
Left from the boot: data that matches nothing else in memory.
Left from the boot: an earlier build of the letter sprites and the title code ($BFE6-$C9FF), the same bytes about $27DB higher.
More of the earlier title code, about $2799 higher than $C467 on.
The end of the earlier title code, $2779 higher than $C887 on.
Left from the boot: an earlier build of the star, keyboard and records code, $24BC higher than $CD44 on.
More of the earlier records code, $2484 higher than $D17C on.
The end of the earlier records code, $2483 higher than $D57D on.
Left from the boot: an earlier copy of the fast loader ($DC00), from $FC89.
The NMI, reset and IRQ vectors as the RAM holds them: with the ROMs out the title ($C540) and the records ($B839) set their own here.
